newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia rebels execute six security officers.
newsitem.headline: Colombia rebels execute six security officers.

text.p: Leftist guerrillas have executed six members of security forces and injured 10 others in a wave of attacks in northern Colombia, authorities said on Wednesday.
The slayings of four policemen and two soldiers took place within the space of 24 hours, authorities said.

Rebels of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) dragged four policemen from their vehicles at a makeshift roadblock near Urrau-Concordia, in northwestern Antioquia province, on Wednesday. The agents, who had been escorting six criminals to a nearby town, were found shot dead later in the afternoon, police said.
There was no word on the fate of the prisoners, none of whom were suspected of rebel-linked activity.

In northeastern Casanare province, National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels pulled two off-duty soldiers off a bus near the town of Hato Corozal on Tuesday afternoon. They were pumped full of bullets while passengers looked on, a police spokesman said.

In neighbouring Arauca province, seven soldiers were injured in an ELN grenade attack, while in northern Santander province three officers suffered shrapnel wounds during a firefight with the FARC. An army spokesman said both incidents took place on Tuesday afternoon.

Arauca has been the scene of intense rebel activity in recent days. The ELN on Sunday and Monday dynamited sections of the country's main oil pipeline which run through the province and prevented engineers from carrying out emergency repairs.
The rebels also announced that they were planning to submit a number of local officials to "people's trials".

In a communique published by some local media on Wednesday, the group admitted responsibility for kidnapping Maria Helena Molina, town mayor of Tame, last month, and said she would be put on political trial before being released.
